issue.title: Bug: test_bgp_update_timer.py fails in L3 scenario due to ExaBGP neighbors flapping

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the bug

The tests `test_bgp_update_timer_single_route`, `test_bgp_update_timer_session_down` consistently fail in **L3 scenario** (`m0_l3_scenario`) but pass in **VLAN scenario** (`m0_vlan_scenario`).

**Test Setup - L3 scenario**:

```
                    ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
                    │              DUT                    │
                    │         (BGP AS 65100)              │
                    │                                     │
                    │   <IP> ◄────────► <IP>      │
                    └───────┬─────────────────────┬───────┘
                            │                     │
                      IN    │                     │    OUT
                      ▲     │                     │     ▼
              ┌─────────────┴──┐               ┌──┴─────────────┐
              │  n0 (ExaBGP)   │               │  n1 (ExaBGP)   │
              │   <IP>     │               │   <IP>     │
              │  (AS 61000)    │               │  (AS 61001)    │
              └────────────────┘               └────────────────┘
```

**Test Setup - VLAN scenario**:

```
                    ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
                    │              DUT                    │
                    │         (BGP AS 65100)              │
                    │                                     │
                    │             <IP>             │
                    └───────┬─────────────────────┬───────┘
                            │                     │
                     IN     │                     │    OUT
                      ▲     │                     │     ▼
              ┌─────────────┴──┐               ┌──┴─────────────┐
              │  n0 (ExaBGP)   │               │  n1 (ExaBGP)   │
              │  <IP>   │               │  <IP>   │
              │  (AS 61000)    │               │  (AS 61001)    │
              └────────────────┘               └────────────────┘
```

**Root Cause:**
- In L3 scenario, the test configures secondary IPv4 address (<IP> and <IP>) on routed interfaces connected to existing ARISTA BGP neighbors.
- In L3 scenario, test creates ExaBGP neighbors (e.g., <IP> and <IP>) and assigns them to the `PEER_V4` peer-group

IP interface config:
```bash
admin@DUT-1:~$ show ip int
Interface       Master    IPv4 address/mask    Admin/Oper    BGP Neighbor    Neighbor IP
--------------  --------  -------------------  ------------  --------------  -------------
Ethernet46                <IP>/31         up/up         ARISTA01MX      <IP>
Ethernet47                <IP>/31         up/up         ARISTA02MX      <IP>
Loopback0                 <IP>/32         up/up         N/A             N/A
PortChannel101            <IP>/31         up/up         ARISTA01M1      <IP>
                          <IP>/31                        pseudoswitch1   <IP>
PortChannel103            <IP>/31         up/up         ARISTA02M1      <IP>
PortChannel105            <IP>/31         up/up         ARISTA03M1      <IP>
PortChannel106            <IP>/31         up/up         ARISTA04M1      <IP>
                          <IP>/31                        pseudoswitch0   <IP>
Vlan1000                  <IP>/24       up/up         N/A             N/A
docker0                   <IP>/24       up/down       N/A             N/A
eth0                      <IP>/24       up/up         N/A             N/A
lo                        <IP>/16         up/up         N/A             N/A
admin@DUT-1:~$
```

BGP peer groups:
```bash
show runningconfig bgp
...
 neighbor <IP> remote-as 61000
 neighbor <IP> peer-group PEER_V4
 neighbor <IP> description pseudoswitch0
 neighbor <IP> timers 3 10
 neighbor <IP> timers connect 10
 neighbor <IP> remote-as 61001
 neighbor <IP> peer-group PEER_V4
 neighbor <IP> description pseudoswitch1
 neighbor <IP> timers 3 10
 neighbor <IP> timers connect 10
```

The `PEER_V4` peer-group has a route-map `TO_BGP_PEER_V4 out` that **permits all routes**:
```bash
route-map TO_BGP_PEER_V4 permit 100
  call CHECK_IDF_ISOLATION
exit
 ...

  neighbor PEER_V4 route-map TO_BGP_PEER_V4 out
```

DUT sends **thousands of routes** learned from ARISTA neighbors to ExaBGP neghbors. ExaBGP cannot handle this flood, causing:
- BGP sessions to flap continuously
- `State/PfxRcd` always flaps between `Idle`, `Active`, or `0` (non-stable neighbors)
- Test assertions to fail because expected BGP UPDATE packets are not captured

**Why L3 scenario fails but VLAN scenario passes:**
In VLAN scenario, ExaBGP neighbors are configured within the `<IP>/24` range on Vlan1000:

```bash
admin@DUT-1:~$ show ip int
Interface       Master    IPv4 address/mask    Admin/Oper    BGP Neighbor    Neighbor IP
--------------  --------  -------------------  ------------  --------------  -------------
Ethernet46                <IP>/31         up/up         ARISTA01MX      <IP>
Ethernet47                <IP>/31         up/up         ARISTA02MX      <IP>
Loopback0                 <IP>/32         up/up         N/A             N/A
PortChannel101            <IP>/31         up/up         ARISTA01M1      <IP>
PortChannel103            <IP>/31         up/up         ARISTA02M1      <IP>
PortChannel105            <IP>/31         up/up         ARISTA03M1      <IP>
PortChannel106            <IP>/31         up/up         ARISTA04M1      <IP>
Vlan1000                  <IP>/24       up/up         pseudoswitch0   <IP>
docker0                   <IP>/24       up/down       N/A             N/A
eth0                      <IP>/24       up/up         N/A             N/A
lo                        <IP>/16         up/up         N/A             N/A
admin@DUT-1:~$
```

**PCAP Evidence:**
- In L3 scenario - captured packets show DUT (<IP>) sending large BGP UPDATE messages with thousands of NLRI entries to ExaBGP (<IP>), causing session instability.
- In VLAN scenario - only desired routes 10.10.100.X/27 announce and withdraw

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Set up a testbed with M0 topology
2. Run test cases:
	- `bgp/test_bgp_update_timer.py::test_bgp_update_timer_single_route[DUT-1-m0_l3_scenario]`
	- `bgp/test_bgp_update_timer.py::test_bgp_update_timer_session_down[DUT-1-m0_l3_scenario]`
3. Observe test failure with errors like:
```bash
==========================================================
FAILED bgp/test_bgp_update_timer.py::test_bgp_update_timer_single_route[DUT-1-m0_l3_scenario] - Failed: no bgp update withdraw route {'prefix': '<IP>/27', 'nexthop': '<IP>'} from <IP> to <IP>
========================================================================================================================== 1 failed, 1 warning in 870.07s (<IPV6>) ==========================================================================================================================
DEBUG:tests.conftest:[log_custom_msg] item: <Function test_bgp_update_timer_single_route[DUT-1-m0_l3_scenario]>
```
```bash
FAILED bgp/test_bgp_update_timer.py::test_bgp_update_timer_single_route[DUT-1-m0_l3_scenario] - Failed: no bgp update announce route {'prefix': '<IP>/27', 'nexthop': '<IP>'} from <IP> to <IP>
========================================================================================================================== 1 failed, 1 warning in 656.74s (<IPV6>) ==========================================================================================================================
DEBUG:tests.conftest:[log_custom_msg] item: <Function test_bgp_update_timer_single_route[DUT-1-m0_l3_scenario]>
```

4. During test execution, check BGP neighbor status on DUT. ExaBGP neighbors (<IP>, <IP>) will show flapping state.
   ```bash

	BGP table version 5641
	RIB entries 2893, using 370304 bytes of memory

	-----------  ---  -----  ---------  ---------  --------  -----  ------  ---------  --------------  --------------
	<IP>      4  65200        858        741      5641      0       0  <IPV6>   1439            ARISTA01M1
	<IP>      4  65200        855        741      5641      0       0  <IPV6>   1439            ARISTA02M1

	<IP>      4  64001        800        741      5641      0       0  <IPV6>   2               ARISTA01MX
	<IP>      4  64002        804        742      5641      0       0  <IPV6>   2               ARISTA02MX
	<IP>       4  61000        264       1914         0      0       0  <IPV6>   Idle            pseudoswitch0
	<IP>       4  61001        532        784      5641      0       0  <IPV6>   0               pseudoswitch1

	Total number of neighbors 8

	IPv4 Unicast Summary:
	BGP router identifier <IP>, local AS number 65100 vrf-id 0
	BGP table version 5641
	RIB entries 2893, using 370304 bytes of memory
	Peers 8, using 192576 KiB of memory
	Peer groups 4, using 256 bytes of memory

	Neighbhor      V     AS    MsgRcvd    MsgSent    TblVer    InQ    OutQ  Up/Down    State/PfxRcd    NeighborName
	-----------  ---  -----  ---------  ---------  --------  -----  ------  ---------  --------------  --------------
	<IP>      4  65200        859        742      5641      0       0  <IPV6>   1439            ARISTA01M1
	<IP>      4  65200        855        742      5641      0       0  <IPV6>   1439            ARISTA02M1
	<IP>      4  65200        851        742      5641      0       0  <IPV6>   1439            ARISTA03M1
	<IP>      4  65200        855        742      5641      0       0  <IPV6>   1439            ARISTA04M1
	<IP>      4  64001        801        742      5641      0       0  <IPV6>   2               ARISTA01MX
	<IP>      4  64002        805        743      5641      0       0  <IPV6>   2               ARISTA02MX
	<IP>       4  61000        264       1914         0      0       0  <IPV6>   Active          pseudoswitch0
	<IP>       4  61001        533        785      5641      0       0  <IPV6>   0               pseudoswitch1

	Total number of neighbors 8
	admin@DUT-1:~$
	```

5. Run the same tests with VLAN scenario - test pass:
- `bgp/test_bgp_update_timer.py::test_bgp_update_timer_single_route[DUT-1-m0_vlan_scenario]`
- `bgp/test_bgp_update_timer.py::test_bgp_update_timer_session_down[DUT-1-m0_vlan_scenario]`

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

**Actual Behavior:**
- DUT floods ExaBGP with thousands of routes from ARISTA neighbors
- In L3 scenario (shared PortChannel interface), ExaBGP sessions flap
- Test fails because expected BGP UPDATE packets are not captured reliably

**Expected Behavior:**
- ExaBGP neighbors should have a route-map that only permits test routes (<IP>/24 range) outbound
- BGP sessions should remain stable throughout the test
- Test should pass consistently in both L3 and VLAN scenarios

**Workaround:**

Manually applying a restrictive route-map on DUT to ExaBGP neighbors after n0, n1 session establishment - fixes the issue:

```bash
vtysh -c "configure terminal" \
      -c "ip prefix-list PL_TEST_ROUTES seq 10 permit <IP>/24 le 32" \
      -c "route-map RM_TEST_ONLY permit 10" \
      -c "match ip address prefix-list PL_TEST_ROUTES" \
      -c "route-map RM_TEST_ONLY deny 20" \
      -c "router bgp 65100" \
      -c "address-family ipv4 unicast" \
      -c "neighbor <IP> route-map RM_TEST_ONLY out" \
      -c "neighbor <IP> route-map RM_TEST_ONLY out"

vtysh -c "clear ip bgp <IP> soft out"
vtysh -c "clear ip bgp <IP> soft out"
```

After applying this, BGP sessions stabilize and the test passes.
```bash
========================================================================================================================= 1 passed, 1 warning in 2637.83s (<IPV6>) ==========================================================================================================================
DEBUG:tests.conftest:[log_custom_msg] item: <Function test_bgp_update_timer_single_route[DUT-1-m0_l3_scenario]>
```

```shell
See logs in bug description and reproduce steps
```

resolution.title: [bgp] Fix BGP update timer test ExaBGP session flapping in L3 scenario (#22391)
resolution.description:
### Description of PR
Fixes https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/issues/22391

#### Summary
When ExaBGP test neighbors are configured on routed interfaces that already have real BGP peers (e.g. M0 L3 scenario with `PEER_V4` peer-group), the DUT floods ExaBGP with thousands of learned routes from the full routing table. ExaBGP cannot handle this volume, causing continuous session flapping and consistent test failures for:
- `test_bgp_update_timer_single_route[*-m0_l3_scenario]`
- `test_bgp_update_timer_session_down[*-m0_l3_scenario]`

#### Root Cause
In L3 scenario, ExaBGP neighbors get added to the `PEER_V4` peer-group which has a permissive outbound route-map (`TO_BGP_PEER_V4`) that advertises all routes. The DUT sends thousands of NLRI entries to ExaBGP, overwhelming it and causing BGP session instability.

#### Fix
After ExaBGP sessions are established, apply a restrictive outbound route-map that only permits test route prefixes (`<IP>/24` for IPv4, `fc00:1x::/48` for IPv6). The route-map is cleaned up in the test teardown.

This approach was validated by the issue reporter as a working workaround.

### Type of change
- [x] Bug fix

### Back port request
- [ ] 202411
- [ ] 202405

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?
The `test_bgp_update_timer` tests consistently fail on M0 L3 topologies because ExaBGP sessions flap under route flooding.

#### How did you do it?
Added helper functions `_apply_outbound_route_filter()` and `_remove_outbound_route_filter()` that:
1. Create a prefix-list matching only test route prefixes
2. Create a route-map that permits only those prefixes
3. Apply the route-map as outbound policy to ExaBGP neighbors
4. Soft-reset BGP so the filter takes effect immediately
5. Clean up everything in the finally block

#### How did you verify/test it?
- Code passes flake8 with max-line-length=120
- Fix matches the exact workaround validated by the issue reporter
- The route-map logic is standard FRR configuration used elsewhere in sonic-mgmt
